assumptions: The source carrier H_N and target class are named before any transfer claim is made.
The circuit model is fixed throughout the transfer, including uniformity and advice conventions.
The transfer from SAT circuits to source-carrier circuits has an explicit exponent envelope q+beta*c+o(1).
Barrier status is route-specific: naturalness, relativization, algebrization, and advice leakage are attached to the actual theorem shape.

calculations.name: Direct-cluster soundness falsifier
calculations.statement: Odd-charge Tseitin-style parity ambiguity is a finite falsifier for local consistency claims that do not bind the target row semantically.
calculations.valid_when: The tested proof system exposes only local projections or bounded-width proof views and lacks a global parity-binding axiom.

definitions.text: A source carrier language, truth-table family, meta-complexity predicate, or proof-mediated object indexed by source length N.
definitions.valid_when: The carrier is explicitly constructed or specified without nonuniform hard-row advice.

definitions.text: The target SAT language or SAT truth-table slice at input length m, used as the reference NP-complete target.
definitions.valid_when: The reduction or transfer states how source length N maps to target length m.

definitions.text: The source lower-bound exponent, overhead exponent, and target-query-length exponent in a transfer inequality.
definitions.valid_when: All padding, decoding, verifier, and advice costs are counted in the same circuit model.

mathematical_object: Target-preserving transfer envelope for P vs NP bridge routes.
non_claims: The paper does not prove P != NP.
The paper does not prove SAT is outside P/poly.
A route-level transfer obstruction is not a target separation theorem.
Artifact evidence documents the run state; external novelty still requires a prior-art boundary.

propositions.name: Bounded-window transfer obstruction
proof_steps: Assume SAT has nonuniform circuits of size n^c in the stated model.
Apply the route transfer to build source-carrier circuits of size N^{q+beta c+o(1)}.
Contradict the source lower bound only for those c with a>q+beta c.
If beta>0, a fixed a excludes at most a bounded exponent window.
propositions.statement: A barely-superlinear source lower bound excludes only the target exponents that fit below the transferred upper-bound envelope.
propositions.valid_when: The source and target circuit models, length map, and overhead exponents are unchanged across the implication.

propositions.latex: \forall c\ \exists N_0\ \forall N\ge N_0:\quad a_c>q_c+\beta_c c
propositions.name: All-exponent lift gate
proof_steps: P/poly exclusion requires ruling out every fixed polynomial exponent c for SAT or an NP-complete target.
For each c, the source lower bound must outrun the transferred upper bound.
If the same source theorem has beta>0 and fixed a, large c survives.
Thus promotion needs beta=0 with positive margin or a cofinal parameter family with no advice leakage.
propositions.statement: A route can support NP not subset P/poly only if it preserves the all-exponent quantifier or supplies a cofinal indexed family.
propositions.valid_when: The parameter family is uniform or advice-accounted and valid on target-relevant lengths.

propositions.name: Searchable certificate gate
proof_steps: State the verifier, decoder, certificate length, and search schedule.
Prove that accepted pairs exist in every required gap interval.
Prove soundness from certificate acceptance to the claimed circuit lower bound.
Audit whether the accepted set is large and constructive, or whether row selection leaks advice.
propositions.statement: A meta-complexity or proof-object bridge is useful only when certificates are frequent, searchable, sound, and advice-free without becoming a large constructive natural property.
propositions.valid_when: The verifier and search live inside the intended target class and do not choose hard rows nonuniformly.

unresolved_obligations: Instantiate one named proof system or meta-complexity carrier and compute q, beta, advice cost, and certificate-search exponent.
Prove the direct-cluster or parity-binding lemma, or exhibit the odd-charge Tseitin counterexample for that named system.
Run a prior-art boundary check against hardness magnification, MCSP/MKtP, natural-proofs, and proof-complexity transfer literature.
State whether the surviving result is a positive bridge theorem, a scoped no-go theorem, or a demoted route diagnostic.
